title: Attachment and Relationships

course_overview.overview: This lesson introduces the core ideas behind attachment and relationships and prepares parents to apply the skills in real-life moments. It blends trauma-informed practice, relational safety, and practical strategies that can be used immediately[cite: 3].

learning_outcomes: Understand the purpose and value of attachment and relationships[cite: 3].
Identify common challenges and how to respond calmly[cite: 3].
Practice simple, repeatable strategies that build confidence[cite: 3].
Strengthen connection and emotional safety during difficult moments[cite: 3].

behavioral_guidelines: Normalize parental struggles and reduce feelings of shame[cite: 3].
Incorporate diverse family dynamics and lived experiences[cite: 3].
Guide participants through emotional safety and co-regulation[cite: 3].

facilitator_dialogue_flow.script: Hello and welcome. Today we are focusing on attachment and relationships, looking at how relational safety forms the foundation of a child's world.

key_concepts: Why attachment and relationships matters for child development[cite: 3].
How trauma and stress impact behaviour[cite: 3].
How parents can model emotional regulation[cite: 3].
Predictability and routine as stabilising tools[cite: 3].
practice_activities: Try a 2-minute grounding exercise before responding to your child[cite: 3].
Practice naming emotions using simple, non-judgemental language[cite: 3].
Role-play a challenging moment and rehearse a calm script[cite: 3].
Identify one routine where attachment and relationships can be used daily[cite: 3].
facilitator_notes: Normalise struggle — parents often feel shame around these skills[cite: 3].
Use examples that reflect diverse families and lived experiences[cite: 3].
Pause often for reflection and emotional processing[cite: 3].
Model co-regulation through tone, pacing, and presence[cite: 3].
reflection_prompts: What part of attachment and relationships feels easiest for me?[cite: 3]
What part feels hardest, and why?[cite: 3]
How did my own childhood shape my reactions?[cite: 3]
What is one small change I can try this week?[cite: 3]
printable_summary:
attachment and relationships — Key Takeaways:
- Stay calm and predictable[cite: 3].
- Use simple language[cite: 3].
- Focus on connection before correction[cite: 3].
- Practice small steps consistently[cite: 3].
